title: Midcycle risk matrix and deployment scribe
body:
Meeting: Midcycle release healthboard sync (standing)
Date: 2025-11-10
Facilitator: Connor Lee
Duration: 45m (ran ~55m)
Location: #release-ops / Zoom

Attendees:
- Connor Lee (RE lead)
- Marta Ruiz (SRE, telemetry)
- Deepak Srinivasan (Serving runtime)
- Jia Chen (Release PM)
- Liam O'Neill (Platform infra)
- Observers: two rotating engineers from Dedicated team

Purpose: quick health check mid-week to identify emergent hotfix candidates, validate canary signals, and surface risks that should block next-stage ramping. Keep decisions lightweight; escalate anything with severity >= P2.

Executive summary:
- Canary for 2025.11.1 rollout showing elevated 99th token-latency in eu-west-1 for long-context models ( > 4k tokens ).
- Two micro-hotfix candidates identified (one config revert, one kernel fallback).
- No customer-facing incidents today, but degraded tail latency correlating with nightly batch compaction jobs on infra nodes.
- Telemetry dashboards updated, but rate-limiting counters missing on a subset of reserved pools (investigating).

Risk heat map (quick):
- Latency tail in eu-west-1 (Severity: Medium-High, Likelihood: High) -> impact: user-facing generation slowdowns, A/B test skewed.
- Autoscaler oscillation when burst > 2x baseline for Dedicated pools (Severity: Medium, Likelihood: Medium) -> impact: cost surge, transient errors.
- KV-cache invalidation edge case during model swap (Severity: Medium-Low, Likelihood: Low) -> impact: rare 5xxs during rollouts.

Risk matrix notes (context + evidence):
- eu-west latency: observed 99p token latency increase from baseline 340ms -> 620ms on long-context routes between 03:00-05:00 UTC. Correlates with nightly compaction job spikes on node drain group c12. See telemetry: panel "token-latency-by-region".
- Autoscaler oscillation: two incidents last sprint where policy thresholds caused scale-down too aggressively; logs show thrashing around watermarks. Autoscale policy currently uses 60s evaluation window.

Hotfix candidates (triaged):
1) Config revert: compaction job schedule moved earlier last deploy (JIRA-RE-1284). Quick revert of compaction window to 06:00-08:00 UTC recommended. Risk: may delay maintenance.
   - Owner: Liam O'Neill
   - Action: schedule revert and run canary in eu-west-1 (small cohort)
   - Target: revert patch by 2025-11-12 02:00 UTC

2) Runtime kernel fallback: certain long-context workloads triggering a quantization kernel path that degrades tail latency (identified in infra PR comment). Temporary fallback to scalar path for affected model family.
   - Owner: Deepak Srinivasan
   - Action: deploy kernel fallback flag, run smoke tests, monitor token-latency and error-rate for 24h
   - Target: toggle by 2025-11-11 22:00 UTC if test pass

3) Rate-limit metrics backfill: missing per-pool counters prevent accurate rate-limit triggered rollbacks. Fix in metrics pipeline PR (GH #762) pending review.
   - Owner: Marta Ruiz
   - Action: prioritize PR review, enable synthetic traffic to validate counters
   - Target: merge by 2025-11-14

Telemetry & signals to watch (quick list):
- token-latency-by-region: 99p and 95p for long-context routes
- reserved-pool-throttle-count: unexpected spikes -> indicates rate-limit misconfigurations
- autoscaler-eval-log: thrash events count > 3 within 10m -> immediate rollback to safe policy
- kv-cache-miss-rate: sudden increase during model swaps -> possible invalidation bug
- error-rate-5xx: correlated with node compactions or kernel fallbacks

Decisions made during meeting:
- Proceed with compaction-schedule revert as immediate hotfix (non-invasive, low-risk).
- Approve guarded kernel fallback in canary cohort (eu-west-1, 5% traffic) for 24h observation. If tail latency improves by >20% without error-rate regressions, expand.
- Hold full ramp in eu-west-1 until the two signals (token-latency and throttle counters) stabilize for 48h.

Action items (owner -> task -> due):
- Liam O'Neill -> revert compaction schedule; coordinate with infra ops to run maintenance window -> 2025-11-12 02:00 UTC
- Deepak Srinivasan -> implement kernel fallback flag + smoke tests, add telemetry hooks to measure kernel path usage -> 2025-11-11 22:00 UTC
- Marta Ruiz -> review metrics PR, create temporary synthetic load job to validate rate-limit counters -> 2025-11-14 12:00 UTC
- Jia Chen -> update rollout plan and canary cohort definition, and notify customer success for any sensitive tenants -> 2025-11-11 18:00 UTC
- Connor Lee -> write post-change checklist and publish in #release-ops, schedule follow-up sync -> 2025-11-12 10:00 UTC

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Consider reducing autoscaler evaluation window from 60s -> 90s for Dedicated pools with variable batched workloads; will reduce thrash but increases reaction time for real load spikes. Need modeling.
- Potential longer-term: implement adaptive compaction windows per-region based on node utilization heatmap. More work but avoids global surprises.
- Is there a way to annotate model variants so telemetry can auto-aggregate long-context vs short-context? Right now panels mix both which hides regressions. TODO: propose schema change.

Open questions / blockers:
- Can CS flag a small set of ecommerce customers as high-risk to exclude from canary? (Jia to confirm)
- Is the cost impact of autoscaler change acceptable for Dedicated pilot customers? (Finance/PM check)

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Quick check-in (15m) tomorrow 2025-11-11 09:30 UTC to validate smoke tests and preliminary telemetry after kernel fallback toggle.
- Full health sync next Monday 2025-11-17 to close the loop on metrics and decide on eu-west-1 ramp schedule.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts referenced:
- JIRA-RE-1284 (compaction-schedule change request)
- JIRA-RE-1297 (kernel-fallback proposal)
- GH #762 (metrics pipeline fix)
- Dashboard: https://dash.redwood-internal/token-latency-by-region
- Runbook: confluence://runbooks/compaction-and-drain

Raw scratch notes captured during sync (unpolished):
- "if we don't revert compaction, may see repeat tail spikes at 03-0500 UTC"
- "kernel path toggles are cheap, rollback leash must be <10m and auto-notify"
- "Marta: need synthetic load harness that mimics long-context token distributions"

End of notes.

Document status: working notes / in_review. Will convert to postmortem template if hotfix executed and results observed (update with data and graphs).
